metadata.title: Channel Theory for Polynomial Continued Fractions: Asymptotic Channels, the ξ₀ = 2/√β₂ Identity, and a Bridge Conjecture
metadata.description:
Version notice (v1.7). This version corrects and attributes; it alters no theorem, proposition or numerical value of v1.6. Concept DOI is preserved (10.5281/zenodo.19941678); v1.6 (10.5281/zenodo.22782807) is superseded. It is a description-only version; the paragraph immediately below states what that means for the attached file.

The file attached to v1.7 is the v1.6 build, unchanged. The v1.7 corrections are recorded in this description only. v1.7 is a description-only new version: no PDF was rebuilt, and none is claimed to have been. The v1.4–v1.6 LaTeX sources are not in the working repository, and the only source held is v1.3.1 — a build made from it would silently revert two versions of corrections, including the Painlevé-target correction made at v1.4 and the analytic residual added at v1.6, both of which this notice relies on. Attaching a build that cannot be verified is the v1.6 defect (1) repeated; not attaching one is the avoidable choice, and it is the one taken. If the v1.6 sources or PDF become available and an updated build is wanted, that is v1.8.

0. Current state

This section is the whole current state. Nothing below it is needed to know what Channel Theory now asserts; §1 is history and §2–§7 are the detail.

Proven. For Q_n = b(n)Q_{n−1} + Q_{n−2} with Q_{−1} = 0, Q_0 = 1, deg b = d ≥ 1 and b(k) ≠ 0 for k ≥ 1:

— the normalised ratio r_n = Q_n/∏_{k≤n} b(k) converges unconditionally, with r_∞ − r_n = O(n^{−(2d−1)});

— if b(n) > 0 for all n ≥ 1 then 1 ≤ r_∞ ≤ exp Σ_{k≥1} 1/(b(k)b(k+1)) < ∞, so the hypothesis (H): r_∞ ≠ 0 holds automatically and is two-sidedly bounded;

— under (H), lim |Q_n/(dn)!|^{1/n} = |β_d|/d^d, hence B(w) = Σ_n Q_n w^n/Γ(dn+1) has radius d^d/|β_d| and, in the uniformiser ζ = w^{1/d}, ξ₀ = d/|β_d|^{1/d};

— Q_n/Γ(dn+1) = K (β_d/d^d)^n n^s (1 + O(1/n)) with s = β_{d−1}/β_d + (d−1)/2.

Attributed, not claimed. The radius identity — i.e. the statement carried since v1.0 as prop:xi0 at d = 2 and promoted at v1.3 to Conjecture 3.3.A★ — is a corollary of the Perron–Kreuser theorem together with Pincherle's minimal/dominant dichotomy. The conjecture label is retired: the statement is not a conjecture, it is classical, and the cross-degree formula ξ₀ = d/|β_d|^{1/d} now holds at every d ≥ 1 as a proved statement rather than at d = 2 proven / d = 4 verified (§2).

Verified, never proven. The closed form K = r_∞ (2π)^{(d−1)/2} / (√d · ∏_i Γ(1 − r_i)), where b(n) = β_d ∏_i (n − r_i) (§4). It agrees with computation to 109–115 decimal digits over eight test polynomials spanning d = 2, 3, 4, with a vacuity control that collapses the agreement to ≤ 0.75 digits when the ∏_i Γ(1 − r_i) factor is removed. It is labelled VERIFIED and must not be written as PROVEN.

Open.

(1) r_∞ itself has no closed form. K isolates the single transcendental input into r_∞; it does not evaluate it.

(2) Whether the exponent s is already in print. The literature route ends at Wong & Li II, which is NOT OBTAINED (§3). The priority position cannot be settled without it, and this notice does not settle it.

(3) A closed form for S_{ζ}. Excluded from one explicitly printed search space (§6.4); not excluded in general. It is carried here under its own new tag, op:cc-szeta-closed-form, and is not filed under op:cc-stokes-closed-form: the latter, created at v1.5 out of the demoted Theorem 3.7(iii), asks whether the CC-channel connection-coefficient *ratio matches the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter, whereas the former asks whether one number admits a multiplicative closed form in a stated basis. Both mention Stokes data; they are different questions, and one name for two objects is the trap §6.0 forbids. The relation between them is stated at §6.4 and is not a merger.

(4) The V_quad normalisation map, which every comparison of Borel-plane constants across the two normalisations still waits on (§6.5). The target is the Painlevé V transcendent on the Sakai surface D₅^(1), and that identification is itself conjectural — the P-III(D₆) naming was corrected at v1.4 and the identification marked conjectural at v1.5. Working material in this repository still says P-III(D₆); it is stale and must not be copied forward.

(5) The singularity type at ξ₀. op:xi0-d3-direct was withdrawn as vacuous at v1.6 — not closed, not answered — and replaced by op:xi0-singularity-type, which is the live problem: the radius is now proved at every d (§2), and the type is untouched by that proof (§5, §8).

(6) Whether the generating-function operator and the V_quad Borel-plane datum determine one another. New at v1.7, and untagged. The operator L_d annihilating Σ_n Q_n z^n has, at d = 2, Katz invariant 1/2 at z = 0 for every admissible coefficient vector, so its multiset always contains 1/2; van der Put–Saito's D̃₅/P_V row prints no 1/2, and the row is therefore excluded outright, together with six others (§7.2, Tier 1, confirmed by two readings of the printed page). The three surviving rows are PIII(D₈), PIII(D₇), PIII(D₆), selected by deg a = 0, 1, 2 (§7.3, Tier 2, self-derived only), with Channel Theory's own a ≡ 1 falling in the first. A matching multiset is necessary, not sufficient: §7 excludes rows and assigns none, so this neither supports nor disputes item 4, and the two have not been shown to be the same object (§7.0, §7.5, §7.6).

Not formalised. The Lean development carries seven sorrys and zero discharged obligations. lake build succeeding shows the statements typecheck; it shows nothing about provability. No result in Channel Theory is machine-checked, and this notice does not claim formal verification.

1. Erratum and version stack

Read downward for history only. Entries for v1.4, v1.5 and v1.6 are quoted from the deposited descriptions of records 20585624, 22717792 and 22782807, fetched on 2026-09-19 — those versions are not in this repository (see the box below).

Version — Version DOI — Published — Disposition

v1.1 — 10.5281/zenodo.19941679 — — — superseded

v1.2 — 10.5281/zenodo.19951331 — — — superseded

v1.3 — 10.5281/zenodo.19972394 — 2026-05-02 — superseded

v1.4 — 10.5281/zenodo.20585624 — 2026-06-07 — superseded

v1.5 — 10.5281/zenodo.22717792 — 2026-09-12 — superseded

v1.6 — 10.5281/zenodo.22782807 — 2026-09-16 — the current published version

v1.7 — — — — — this notice

The concept record 10.5281/zenodo.19941678 currently resolves to version 1.6, and DataCite lists exactly the six HasVersion identifiers above, so v1.7 is the correct next version number. (Read 2026-09-19 from the concept record and the v1.6 record, both listed in §10; the concept DOI is taken from the conceptdoi / parent field, never from a record number.)

v1.1 → v1.2. The v1.1 cross-degree candidate c(d) = 2√((d−1)!) — which agrees with d = 2 by coincidence — was empirically falsified at d = 4: it predicts ≈ 4.899 against a measured 4, ≈ 22 % disagreement (Remark 3.3.E).

v1.3 (2026-05-02). Purely additive framing revision; nothing rewritten or retracted. Added §3.5 (rem:h4-median), §3.6, and op:cc-median-resurgence-execute. Promoted the cross-degree formula to Conjecture 3.3.A★, ξ₀(b) = d/β_d^{1/d}, proven at d = 2, verified at d = 4, d = 3 deferred to op:xi0-d3-direct.

v1.4 (2026-06-07) — two corrections. (1) The EBR ξ₀ upgrade. For positivity families b(n) > 0 (n ≥ 1), the identity ξ₀ = d/β_d^{1/d} was proved for the physical generating-function object by the holonomic/positivity argument of the companion EBR preprint 10.5281/zenodo.20564079 §3 (D-finite G; leading coefficient a_{2d}(s) = d^d s^{2d}(d^d − β_d s), roots {0, R}; Pringsheim), with scope positive-b families, physical object, symbolic + verified-to-d6 + Lean-checked algebraic layer d = 2–5, not a symbolic-degree formal proof. That superseded the Conjecture-3.3.A★ status for the positive-b case only. (2) Surface-type correction. All references — body, keywords and description — were corrected from Painlevé III(D₆) to the Painlevé V transcendent on the Sakai surface D₅^(1) (W(A₃^(1)), δ = −1/2 ≠ 0). Channel Theory was the last deposit carrying the stale P-III(D₆) root claim.

v1.5 (2026-09-12) — a demotion. Clause (iii) of Theorem 3.7, the match between the CC-channel connection-coefficient ratio and the Riemann–Hilbert datum of P_V/D₅^(1) at the V_quad τ-parameter, is not a theorem of this paper and became the open problem op:cc-stokes-closed-form. Two grounds: the imported surface-type premise is itself conjectural (companion paper Conjecture 4.1, 10.5281/zenodo.20455089, read at v1.2), and the cited run stores a comparison its own verdict did not incorporate — a factor of about two accounted for by an explicit halving in the source, with ~1.7 % unexplained. v1.5 also withdrew as non-evidential a Domb–Sykes sentence that rounded two endpoints agreeing to two digits into a three-digit "range", and corrected five citations that pinned a version in which the cited object was not yet a conjecture. The v1.4 sentence "both corrections are additive/clarifying; no … claim is retracted" does not describe v1.5.

v1.6 (2026-09-16) — five defects repaired; a build, labelling and open-problem erratum. (1) The v1.5 PDF was the draft build, watermarked "DRAFT — NOT DEPOSITED", its date line stalled at "2026-06-07 (v1.4, draft)" and its changelog ending at v1.3 — front matter, not text. (2) op:xi0-d3-direct withdrawn as vacuous, replaced by op:xi0-singularity-type, with rem:d3-vacuous recording the withdrawal (see §5). (3) A citation gap: 10.5281/zenodo.20542162 (deposited 2026-06-04) derives the slope-1/d edge polynomial χ_d(c) = 1 + (−1)^{d+1}(β_d/d^d) c^d symbolically and d-free for all d ≥ 2, with only β_d appearing on the edge; it is now cited at Conjecture 3.3.A★ and op:xi0-degree-d, and that problem is restated — no per-degree computation remains, and the residual is analytic rather than algebraic. (4) Every cross-reference to a proposition, conjecture, remark, definition, example or open problem rendered as "Theorem N" in v1.0–v1.5 (110 sites), because the environments share one counter; the numbered blocks themselves were always correct. Readers of v1.0–v1.5 must treat "Theorem N.N" in running text as naming whatever class the numbered block declares. (5) Falsifiers added to op:cc-median-resurgence-execute and op:cc-formal-borel, the former also gaining a vacuity pre-check — hold β₂ fixed, vary the lower-order coefficients, and confirm that S_{ζ*} actually moves — and all surviving §9 cost estimates marked unverified.

v1.7 (this notice) changes five things.

(1) §2 Attribution. Conjecture 3.3.A★ is retired and attributed. This replaces the v1.4 EBR grounding, which held only for positive b and only for the physical object; the classical route needs no positivity hypothesis at all.

(2) §3 The exponent. s = β_{d−1}/β_d + (d−1)/2 is stated with its derivation and its priority position, including that Wong & Li II is NOT OBTAINED.

(3) §4 K and r_∞. The closed form, and r_∞ identified as exactly the constant the classical turning-point method normalises out of view.

(4) §5 The vacuity explanation. A one-line structural reason generalising and de-empiricising rem:d3-vacuous: v1.6 established the phenomenon for ξ₀ by a coefficient sweep; §5 derives it for ξ₀ and ρ from two proved statements, with no sweep.

(5) §6 The Borel material. ζ* = 2ξ₀ is an action difference, not a change of variable; op:cc-median-resurgence-execute is restated to name the series it concerns; and a pre-registered negative result is recorded against a search space printed in full, filed under a new tag op:cc-szeta-closed-form kept deliberately separate from op:cc-stokes-closed-form (§0, §6.4).

### What was fetched, and what still was not Channel Theory v1.4, v1.5 and v1.6 are not in this repository — the newest in-repo source is v1.3.1, and the v1.3.1 claims record points at pcf-research/channel/…, which does not exist on this machine. The deposited descriptions were therefore fetched from the records themselves on 2026-09-19 with their bytes and hashes recorded in §10: v1.5 and v1.6 from the Zenodo API, v1.3 and v1.4 from DataCite after zenodo.org began returning HTTP 504 on every further request. Everything in the stack above is quoted from that deposited text. Still not obtained, and therefore not quoted: * The v1.5 and v1.6 PDFs. Both file endpoints returned HTTP 504 (api/ records/…/files/…/content and the classic records/…/files/…?download=1). So §9's falsifier statements and their numeric thresholds have not been read — v1.6's description says both open problems now carry one, and §6.3 below says only that, not what the threshold is. * The v1.4 description may be partial. DataCite returned a single 5808-byte description for it; the Zenodo record carries the full HTML, which could not be fetched. The v1.4 text quoted above is also retained verbatim inside the v1.6 description, which is the copy actually used. A correction to this session's own earlier finding. Before the records were fetched, op:xi0-singularity-type was reported as having zero occurrences and was not cited. That was true of the repository and false of the corpus: the tag was created at v1.6 and is real. A repo-wide search establishes absence from the repo, not absence from the published record.

2. Attribution: Conjecture 3.3.A★ is not a conjecture

The statement. With b(n) = β_d n^d + …, β_d ≠ 0, b(k) ≠ 0 for k ≥ 1:

Displayed: lim_{n→∞} | Q_n / (dn)! |^{1/n} = |β_d| / d^d,

so B(w) = Σ_{n≥0} Q_n w^n / Γ(dn+1) has radius of convergence d^d/|β_d| in w, and in the uniformiser ζ = w^{1/d}

Displayed: ξ₀ = d / |β_d|^{1/d}, and at d = 2, ξ₀ = 2/√β₂.

This is prior art. Write the recurrence in the classical form Q_{n+1} + a_n Q_n + b_n Q_{n−1} = 0 with a_n = −b(n+1) ∼ −β_d n^d and b_n = −1, so that in Gautschi's notation α = d and β = 0. Hypotheses (2.2) and (2.8) hold, and the Newton–Puiseux vertex P₁ = (1, d) lies above the segment P₀ = (0,0) — P₂ = (2,0) for every d ≥ 1, so case (a) applies and the ratio asymptotics follow.

Cited to: W. Gautschi, Computational aspects of three-term recurrence relations, SIAM Review 9 (1967), Theorem 2.3(a), p. 35 (Perron–Kreuser) and Theorem 1.1, p. 31 (Pincherle); DLMF §3.6(ii) for the same dichotomy. Both were read from the sources themselves, including a page image of p. 35; see the bibliography in §10.

Gautschi's condition (2.8) constrains the exponents α, β to be real. It does not constrain the coefficients, so complex β_d is inside the classical statement.

Retire the conjecture label. Conjecture 3.3.A★ asserted ξ₀(b) = d/β_d^{1/d} for every degree-d PCF in scope, with the status proven at d = 2, verified at d = 4, d = 3 deferred. That tiered status is withdrawn. The identity holds at every d ≥ 1, classically by Perron–Kreuser plus Pincherle, and independently by an elementary proof carried in the AEAL record — thm:radius, proved without Gamma asymptotics, its Step 3 using a combinatorial multinomial sandwich rather than Stirling (PROVEN). Both routes need only (H): r_∞ ≠ 0.

This supersedes, for this purpose, the EBR positivity upgrade as the grounding. The v1.4 grounding (10.5281/zenodo.20564079 §3) proves the identity only for positivity families b(n) > 0 (n ≥ 1), only for the physical generating-function object, and with a Lean-checked algebraic layer covering d = 2–5 — by its own §8 scope statement, not a symbolic-degree formal proof. The route stated here needs no positivity hypothesis, is not restricted to the physical object, and carries no degree ceiling; the EBR argument remains a valid independent proof on its own narrower scope and is not withdrawn. What (H) asserts is exactly that Q_n is not the minimal solution of the recurrence; the minimal subspace has codimension one, so (H) is generic. That Pincherle reading is interpretive and load-bearing on nothing (STRUCTURAL). Positivity of b re-enters only as the cheapest sufficient condition for (H): if b(n) > 0 for all n ≥ 1 then r_n is strictly increasing with r_n ≥ 1 (PROVEN), and it is then also bounded above by exp Σ_{k≥1} 1/(b(k)b(k+1)) (PROVEN), the positivity being load-bearing in that bou
